Convert a Word or PowerPoint file to Markdown

convert_markdown.Rd

Uses Pandoc to turn a .docx or .pptx file into Markdown, keeping headings, lists, tables, footnotes and citations, and saving the images into a media/ folder. Run clean_markdown() on the result next.

Usage

convert_markdown(
  input_file,
  markdown_file = "markdown_output.md",
  media_base_dir = ".",
  pandoc_args = NULL,
  pandoc_version = "default",
  verbose = FALSE,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

input_file

Path to the .docx or .pptx file.

markdown_file

Path for the Markdown file. Defaults to "markdown_output.md".

media_base_dir

Folder to save images in. Pandoc creates a media/ folder inside it, but only if the document has images. Defaults to ".", the working directory. Use NULL to skip saving images.

pandoc_args

Extra Pandoc arguments, as a string or character vector, for example "--wrap=none", or "-t gfm" for tables with long text. Some Markdown flavours add escaping to citations, which clean_markdown(clean_citations = TRUE) removes. Defaults to NULL.

pandoc_version

Which Pandoc to use, passed to pandoc::pandoc_run(). Defaults to "default". If that Pandoc is missing or older than 3.8.3 (needed for PowerPoint), the one bundled with RStudio, Positron or Quarto is used instead.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print the Pandoc command and where images were saved. Defaults to FALSE.

overwrite

Logical. If FALSE, stop rather than write over an existing markdown_file. Defaults to TRUE. Use timestamped_path() to keep earlier versions.

Value

Invisibly, a list with markdown_file (the path to the Markdown) and media_dir (the path to the media/ folder, or NULL if no images were saved).

See also

Other workflow: clean_markdown(), replace_placeholders(), run_workflow()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
convert_markdown("draft.docx", markdown_file = "draft.md")
convert_markdown("slides.pptx", markdown_file = "slides.md", media_base_dir = "slides")
} # }
